prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In frames 1 and 2, the depth map shows the camera wearer's extended left arm and hand in the near foreground (0.2 to 0.6 m) holding a vertical measuring tape against a metallic grid wall sculpture mounted on a flat wall roughly 0.6 to 0.8 m directly in front. Across frames 3 and 4, as the camera wearer turns rightward toward an interior wall corner and pitches downward, the map captures the converging left and right wall planes (0.5 to 1.2 m away) and a small white stand below with a tall bottle-shaped vase, a round white vase, and a small plant within arm's reach (0.6 to 1.0 m), with a dark doorway gap visible on the far right of frame 3. In frame 5, a near wall edge on the left (around 0.3 to 0.5 m) partially occludes an adjacent living room to the right, where a blue accent chair stands roughly 2.5 to 3.0 m away in front of a glass coffee table and a light-coloured couch at 3.5 to 4.5 m; no other people are present in the scene. The depth map makes the 3D relief of the thin metal grid rods, the orthogonal corner geometry of the featureless white walls, and the abrupt depth discontinuity at the frame 5 wall boundary much clearer than the RGB strip alone. However, the map is unreliable in absolute scale continuity across frames—rendering the wall at 0.7 m in frames 1–2 much darker than the corner walls at a similar distance in frames 3–4—and loses the thin legs of the distant chair and fine foliage details in frames 3–5.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map detects only the camera wearer's extended left arm and hand as a pink 'person' mask in the lower-left foreground (0.2 to 0.6 m away, within immediate reach) in frames 1 and 2, where the arm partially occludes the vertical measuring tape and metal wall grid directly behind it. Frames 3 and 4 contain no segmented masks at all as the camera turns right to face the wall corner and the small white corner table with vases and greenery roughly 0.6 to 1.0 m below and in front of the wearer. In frame 5, as the viewpoint pans past the near left wall edge into the open room, the map segments the blue accent chair (green 'chair' mask, about 2.5 to 3.0 m away to the right-centre) and the sofa behind it (brown 'couch' mask, about 3.5 to 4.5 m away in the upper right, roughly 1.0 to 1.5 m behind the chair and partially cut off by the top and right frame borders). The map clearly isolates the foreground arm silhouette and separates the overlapping boundary where the accent chair sits in front of and partially occludes the couch in frame 5, whereas no other people are present or facing the camera wearer. It is unreliable for broader scene layout because it completely misses the measuring tape, wall sculpture, walls, corner stand, vases, plant, and coffee table across all frames, and truncates the lower ends of the chair's thin metal legs in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank in frames 1, 2, 3, and 5, containing only a single small yellow body-skeleton fragment near the bottom-centre of frame 4. In frames 1 and 2, the camera wearer's own extended left arm and hand (0.2 to 0.6 m in front of the lens, holding the tape against the wall grid within arm's reach) enter from the lower-left edge with the torso out of view, and no other people are present in any of the five frames. As the camera turns rightward and tilts down toward the corner table (0.6 to 1.0 m away) in frame 4, the yellow skeleton in the pose map is a false-positive detection hallucinated on the rounded white vase and small plant foliage at the bottom of the frame rather than an actual person facing or looking toward the wearer. Because this only skeleton detection is spurious and all magenta hand keypoints and yellow arm keypoints for the wearer's visible left limb in frames 1 and 2 are missing, the pose map is entirely unreliable here and adds no valid spatial information beyond the RGB frames.
